hook.text: A turbocharger turns exhaust waste into extra power—free energy from stuff you'd throw away.

buildup.text: Exhaust gases spin a turbine at up to 150,000 RPM. That turbine drives a compressor on a shared shaft.

discovery.text: The compressor forces extra air into the engine. More air means more fuel can burn, so more power.

twist.text: Turbo lag is the delay before the turbine spins fast enough. You press the gas and wait a beat.

climax.text: Modern twin-scroll and electric turbos nearly eliminate lag, giving instant response.
